Let me analyze this conflict.

The certificate document says the applicant is "Hottinger Brüel & Kjaer GmbH" while the register says "Hottinger Baldwin Messtechnik GmbH".

This is not spelling drift — these are genuinely different company names. Hottinger Baldwin Messtechnik (HBM) rebranded as Hottinger Brüel & Kjaer (HBK) around 2019-2020 after HBM merged with Brüel & Kjær Sound & Vibration under Spectris. So in 2021, the legal entity name would be Hottinger Brüel & Kjaer GmbH. The certificate is the legal instrument, dated 2021, and it names "Hottinger Brüel & Kjaer GmbH".

Per the rules: "Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity (best_value = the document's, since the certificate is the legal instrument)."

Even though they're historically the same company (rebrand), the rule says genuinely different company names = different-entity with document's value. The names are clearly different — "Baldwin Messtechnik" vs "Brüel & Kjaer". This isn't spelling drift or suffix drift. So verdict: different-entity, best_value: "Hottinger Brüel & Kjaer GmbH".

The why: The document's name is a distinct legal name (post-rebrand HBK), not a spelling variant of the register's HBM name, so the certificate's own legal instrument wins.
